blocks.raw:
<LawCallout code="pd1096" section="Rule I - General Provisions">


⚠️ Common mistake: Do not apply the 1200 mm ramp width (Appendix A) to sidewalks/walkways — those require 1500 mm minimum (Appendix B). Each BP 344 element has its own dimension. Mixing them is a frequent exam trap.


</LawCallout>

blocks.raw:
<LawCallout code="bp344">

Golden Rule: BP 344 is a special law (lex specialis). For accessible routes, BP 344's stricter dimensional standards prevail over PD 1096's general minimums. The key exam principle: know which law governs which element.

</LawCallout>

blocks.raw:
<ExamTip>

LEA Trap: The exam often tests ramp width. PD 1096 says 'as wide as corridor' (min 1.10 m). BP 344 Appendix A says 1.20 m min for accessible ramps. The correct LEA answer for an accessible ramp is 1.20 m — always apply the stricter BP 344 standard.

</ExamTip>

blocks.raw:
<LawCallout code="bp344" section="Section 4 - Prevailing Law">


📌 Exam Tip: The LEA frequently tests the BP 344 ramp width (1200 mm) vs. sidewalk width (1500 mm) distinction in scenario-based questions. Remember: ramp = 1200 mm, sidewalk = 1500 mm, rest space = 1800 mm. These three numbers appear together in integrated compliance questions.


</LawCallout>
